title: Shockley-Queisser limit
references: Shockley, W. and Queisser, H. J., Detailed Balance Limit of Efficiency of p-n Junction Solar Cells, Journal of Applied Physics 32(3), 510-519 (1961), doi:10.1063/1.1736034
Rühle, S., Tabulated values of the Shockley-Queisser limit for single junction solar cells, Solar Energy 130, 139-147 (2016), doi:10.1016/j.solener.2016.02.015
De Vos, A., Detailed balance limit of the efficiency of tandem solar cells, Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics 13(5), 839-846 (1980), doi:10.1088/0022-3727/13/5/018
validity_domain: Power conversion efficiency of a single-junction solar cell under unconcentrated sunlight (AM1.5G, cell at 300 K): at most 33.7 %, the detailed-balance maximum over all band gaps (reached near 1.34 eV). The limit of any particular material, silicon included, is lower or equal.
limitations: Assumption cell_type: for a single-junction cell under unconcentrated sunlight the bound is 33.7 %; for multi-junction (tandem) cells or concentrated sunlight the bound used is 86.8 %, the detailed-balance limit of an infinite stack of junctions under maximum concentration (De Vos 1980).
The maximum over band gaps is used, so the bound never exceeds what any single-junction material allows; it is not the lower limit of a specific material
Hot-carrier, multiple-exciton and up/down-conversion schemes are outside its assumptions
